implement: legion-worker: the phase mechanics, the implementer's proof rules (pr-body.md) and the push/handoff procedure every commit of this change follows
dispatch: the two operator asks (stage 4a on the devbox, the production boot) and the preconditions of §6 are Dispatch writes
test: legion-worker: the tester's proof and what it re-runs are defined in references/pr-body.md; the tester drives §5's surfaces and CI's statics
dispatch: a finding or a blocked proof goes to the issue as the skill says
review: legion-worker: the review order and the merge gate (references/merge-gate.md, review-threads.md)
thermonuclear-deep-review: the change touches authentication paths (lenient body reads, refusals) and the daemon's relaunch loop; a correctness and security audit of the diff

findings.finding: Which binary the LEGION deployment's daemon runs (release archive, deployment-repo build, or the worker image whose legion links only main.revision) cannot be established here, so the release-linked plugin versions may never reach it.
findings.answer: Asked the architect over Envoy; answer 2026-10-12T20:13Z: assume it may be the worker image's legion. D9 links the pair into both the release archive and the worker image (release-only build-args from the plugin jobs' outputs) and makes `legion version`, `--check-config` and the boot log print the pair or `none`; §6 reads it from the deployed daemon before the restart and sets runtime.kubernetes.plugins by dispatch ask when it prints none.

findings.finding: 'The daemon knows no plugin versions: charged as a launch failure' would, at the first boot on this release where every claim is stale, burn every claim's launch budget in launch()'s retry loop (machine.go:839-846) and end the fleet in worker-died.
findings.answer: D5: a kubernetes daemon with no source records, writes one Error per stale claim naming runtime.kubernetes.plugins, relaunches nothing and refuses nothing; --check-config and boot name the gap; TestAKubernetesDaemonWithNoPluginSourceRelaunchesNothing. Recorded as spec departure 1.

findings.finding: Answering a stale registration with 409 reads against the spec's Rejected row, whose premise (the plugin's exit counts as a death) is contradicted by the fences (machine.go:698-707) and the runtime's own stop (relaunch.go:148-155).
findings.answer: D4 records, relaunches, then answers 409; the fence evidence is cited and the departure recorded (spec departure 2) for the architect to amend the row or hold the plan to a 200.

findings.finding: Keying the install to the claim's recorded contract installs into a pod replaced for a reason other than drift (suspended Sandbox, lost binding, failed init, moved address), contradicting 'a launch for any other reason installs nothing'.
findings.answer: D7: Plugins travels in the SpawnSpec, drift alone no longer forces replace when it is set, and the runtime installs only on the kept-pod path; a replaced pod is on the configured image, which the boot gate holds to the daemon's contract. T5 tests the three cases.

findings.finding: specs.SpawnSpec returns controllerSpawnSpec() before reading the claim (specs.go:59-61), so the daemon-launched controller's relaunch would carry no install and be charged until failed.
findings.answer: D7/T4: the controller branch takes the claim and Plugins is computed before it; T2 adds the stale daemon-launched controller test.

findings.finding: One lenient field list cannot identify the caller on /grants (claim form matches sessionId+tree+issue, then the secret) nor on register (boot token), and the refusal shape differs per route family; the body carries secrets.
findings.answer: D6: a per-route identity map ({bootToken}, {claimToken,secret}, {sessionId,secret,tree,issue}, {sessionId,secret}, {grantId}), authenticated as the route would; errorBody vs Failure{STALE_PLUGIN_CONTRACT} per family; the register route decodes leniently from the start; the body is never logged.

findings.finding: An install failure arrives as the process gone (died → relaunchAfterFailure), not as a Spawn/Resume refusal; the wrapper's stdout would pollute the shim's frame stream; the agent argv must survive quoting.
findings.answer: D8: the install section is grouped and redirected 1>&2, the agent argv rides as positional parameters after `exec "$@"`, and the plan states the death path charges LaunchFailures (the Deaths budget is untouched for an unready claim, table.go:378); the retry keeps the pod because the recorded contract still differs.

findings.finding: Stage 4a has no daemon and a stub agent that never registers, so acceptance 4's 'registered contract' is unprovable there, and the script is devbox-only.
findings.answer: T8 reads the installed pi-legion's legion.daemonApiVersion in the generation directory against the rig's contract (spec departure 3) and the run is an operator step by dispatch ask (D12, §6).

findings.finding: Acceptance 7's read_record reads GET /legion/v1/state, which authenticates nobody, so it discriminates nothing; the rest of the criterion needs production kubectl and the daemon log.
findings.answer: §6: the relaunched role's next bash call (a grant on POST /legion/v1/grants) and read_record showing pluginContract and the unchanged podUid; operator steps as one dispatch ask per step with exact commands. Spec departure 5.

findings.finding: Making `legion` need pi_legion naively skips the daemon release on daemon-only runs, and a green pi_legion that published nothing has an empty version output.
findings.answer: D9: legion keeps its own if and adds always() && (result == success || skipped) for both plugin jobs; each version is the job output else `jq -r .version packages/pi-<name>/package.json`; the job fails when either is empty.

findings.finding: Printing the plugin versions from `legion version` breaks the release smoke test (release.yaml:308) and the image check (worker.Dockerfile:640-641), which assert the one line verbatim.
findings.answer: D9/T6: the first line is unchanged, the second appears only when a pair is linked, and both checks compare line by line (exactly one line when no pair is linked).

findings.finding: The worker-image ldflags have no known consumer unless the production daemon is the image's legion.
findings.answer: Kept on the architect's instruction (the production daemon may be the image's legion); build-args are optional so a pull-request image links none.

findings.finding: Stage 4b's branch-built daemon has no plugin versions, and its checkpoints read --check-config output and open capability rows.
findings.answer: T7: stage 4b's config gains plugins: naming the run's packed tarballs' in-pod paths (never installed); the gap is a plain line, kubernetes-only, so check-config-passes (tmux) is untouched; restart-mid-tree holds because every 4b claim registers at the branch daemon's contract.

findings.finding: 'Contract discipline' lives in the historical TypeScript-daemon section (docs/kubernetes.md:1992, :2494-2500); the Go-daemon section has none; the 'never from an npm release' sentence (:101-104) becomes misleading.
findings.answer: T7 and spec departure 4: a new Contract discipline subsection in the Go-daemon section beside 'Pinning a release…', the historical one loses the two sentences and points to it, the npm sentence is qualified.

findings.finding: Loop prevention rests on LaunchFailures never being reset, and the life of PluginRelaunchFor is unstated.
findings.answer: D1/D4: PluginRelaunchFor is set at every stale relaunch and cleared when a registration records the daemon's contract; the invariant (a stale registration never reaches ready at its generation) is stated and TestARelaunchedProcessStillStaleIsChargedUntilWorkerDied drives three stale registrations to failed.

findings.finding: runtime.kubernetes.plugins: partial blocks, mixed sources and what --check-config can validate are unspecified.
findings.answer: D9: both keys or neither (a half block refused naming the missing key), a dist-tag or range refused; --check-config validates presence and shape and prints the pair; a tarball path's readability inside a pod is unverifiable from the daemon and is left to the install's own failure line.

findings.finding: How pluginContract 0 appears on the wire is unspecified and the TS mirrors are strict.
findings.answer: D10: always emitted, 0 = no contract recorded, z.number().int().nonnegative() with that comment; fixtures regenerated by the Go golden tests.

findings.finding: 'every pod has bun and npm' is verified for the current image only; the pods this change rescues run older images.
findings.answer: D8 calls /usr/local/bin/bun by absolute path and names the failure mode (the death path, visible in the pod log); §6 precondition 3 checks the oldest live pod before the restart.

findings.finding: 'nowhere extension discovery reads, so no plugin loads twice' rests on Oh My Pi behaviour outside this repository.
findings.answer: §5 row 4(c): `legion probe-image` run in the pod with --plugin-root/--envoy-plugin-root naming the installed generation copies proves the pair loads once through the pod lane; listed under risks.

findings.finding: 'a pi-legion beside a pi-envoy at another interface version refuses to start' was not cited.
findings.answer: Cited: packages/pi-legion/extensions/legion.ts:94-102 and packages/pi-shared/src/interface.ts:19 (§1, §3).

findings.finding: 'pi-legion exits on a 4xx registration' is verified at HEAD only; older plugins may not.
findings.answer: D4 states nothing depends on the exit: the runtime stops the earlier generation (relaunch.go:148-152; tmux kills the pane) and the old incarnation's observations are fenced.

findings.finding: Three load-bearing spec claims are supported and should be cited rather than restated (refusal surfaced verbatim, the sentence is a contract item, the per-generation environment is re-sent).
findings.answer: Cited in §1 and D4/D6; the new sentences go into pi-legion's changelog (T1).

findings.finding: Acceptance 6, 5 and 4 have no command whose output decides them.
findings.answer: §5 row 6 gives the greps (two sentences absent, the relaunch line present twice, the generation directory in the opening note); D4/D6 fix the refusal sentences verbatim and the api tests assert them; T5/T8 assert no Sandbox suspend, no provision call, same pod uid and creationTimestamp.

specDepartures.spec: Errors table, 'The daemon knows no plugin versions: built from an unreleased commit, with no runtime.kubernetes.plugins': 'A stale launch cannot be built: charged as a launch failure naming the missing setting; legion start --check-config names it as an open gap before any launch.'
specDepartures.plan: D5: a kubernetes daemon with no plugin source records contracts, writes one Error line per stale claim at boot and at each stale registration naming runtime.kubernetes.plugins, relaunches nothing and refuses no decodable call; --check-config prints the gap after its OK line and boot logs it. Under tmux nothing degrades.
specDepartures.evidence: launch() retries a refused spec at once and fails the claim at Limits.LaunchFailures (internal/supervise/machine.go:839-846); at the first boot on this release every live claim has no recorded contract, so the spec's row would end every live claim in worker-died within seconds of the boot meant to rescue them.

outcome.scope: The Errors row 'The daemon knows no plugin versions' and the sentence in 'What changes' that a stale launch without versions is charged.

specDepartures.spec: Rejected: 'Refuse the registration of a stale process instead of recording and relaunching it: the plugin exits on a refused registration, which the daemon counts as a death; recording and relaunching keeps it uncharged and gives the operator the same log line.'
specDepartures.plan: D4: the registration is recorded and the process relaunched (uncharged the first time), and the answer is then a 409 naming both contracts and that the daemon is relaunching the process, so the pod's own log says why the process ends.
specDepartures.evidence: After the relaunch the claim is at its next generation: a Gone observation of the old incarnation is dropped as stale (internal/supervise/machine.go:698-707), ready/exit from it are fenced (machine.go:776-786), and the Sandbox runtime stops the earlier generation before starting the next (internal/runtime/sandbox/relaunch.go:148-152); pi-legion exits on a 4xx registration answer (packages/pi-legion/src/claim-session.ts:58-66), which is an optimisation nothing depends on.

outcome.scope: The Rejected row's wording: what is rejected is refusing without recording and relaunching; the refusal issued after both is the plan's answer.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 4's check: a stage 4a checkpoint 'relaunches one role as stale, and reads the pod's uid unchanged, the new generation's registered contract, and its Oh My Pi's --extension arguments naming the generation directory.'
specDepartures.plan: T8: the checkpoint reads the installed pi-legion's legion.daemonApiVersion in <gen dir>/node_modules/@sjawhar/pi-legion/package.json and compares it with the contract the rig configured, beside the unchanged pod uid and creationTimestamp, the never-suspended Sandbox and the stub agent's --extension arguments; registration is proved by the fake-runtime daemon tests (acceptance 3) and in production (acceptance 7).
specDepartures.evidence: Stage 4a drives sandbox.Runtime directly with a stub agent that never registers and no daemon API (internal/runtime/sandbox/live_test.go:203, runtimeOptions :767-788; an in-memory store).

outcome.acceptance: 4: 'the new generation's registered contract' becomes 'the installed pi-legion's declared daemon API contract equals the one the rig configured'.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 6: 'Contract discipline' and 'Pinning a release that drops what a running pod still uses' each quote the boot's relaunch line and describe the install in the kept pod; the opening note names the generation directory.
specDepartures.plan: T7: a new 'Contract discipline' subsection in the Go-daemon section of docs/kubernetes.md beside 'Pinning a release…' carries the text; the historical 'Contract discipline' loses its two sentences and points to the new one; the sentence 'One commit ⇒ one image: Legion's own plugins come from the commit, never from an npm release' is qualified for a relaunched role.
specDepartures.evidence: docs/kubernetes.md:2494-2500 sits inside '## Kubernetes runtime (TypeScript daemon)' (:1992: 'which it no longer runs … the section goes with packages/daemon at Stage 7'); the Go-daemon section has no contract-discipline passage; :101-104 states the plugins never come from npm.

outcome.acceptance: 6: the passage quoting the relaunch line is the new Go-daemon 'Contract discipline' subsection (and 'Pinning a release…'); the historical heading is reduced to a pointer; the 'never from an npm release' sentence is qualified.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 7: '… one relaunched role's Oh My Pi process carries --extension arguments naming its generation directory …, and that role's next legion tool call (its read_record) succeeds.'
specDepartures.plan: §6: the relaunched role's next bash tool call succeeds (it mints a grant on POST /legion/v1/grants, the call that failed on 2026-10-12) and its read_record shows its own claim's pluginContract equal to the daemon's with the podUid recorded before the restart; the operator steps run as one dispatch ask each with exact commands.
specDepartures.evidence: read_record reads GET /legion/v1/state, which authenticates nobody and which this change refuses for no one (internal/api/server.go:225; the spec's own 'GET /legion/v1/state authenticates nobody'), so a stale process's read_record succeeds too.

outcome.acceptance: 7: 'that role's next legion tool call (its read_record) succeeds' becomes 'that role's next bash call mints a grant and its read_record shows its pluginContract equal to the daemon's'.
